title: CI Hugging Face datasets cache (cache-hf action): restore-only callers never save, and each runner.os key needs exactly one saving job
answers: Why do protobuf cross-test or test-requirements CI jobs no longer write the Hugging Face datasets cache?
How do I make a new CI workflow use the Hugging Face datasets cache without it overwriting the shared cache?
Which workflow is responsible for saving the HF datasets cache for Linux and Windows runners in CI?
Where is the restore-only option for the cache-hf composite action defined?
body:
Path: .github/actions/cache-hf/action.yml (composite action, the chokepoint for CI caching of the Hugging Face hub datasets directory ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/datasets--*) is used by test workflows (master, slow-tests, protobuf-cross-test, test-requirements) to avoid Hugging Face 429 rate limits.
Rule: The action takes an optional `restore-only` input (default "false"). When it is "true", the step uses `actions/cache/restore` and never saves; otherwise it uses `actions/cache` (restore + save). Path, key (`${{ runner.os }}-hf-datasets-${{ hashFiles('tests/data/test_huggingface_dataset_and_source.py') }}`) and restore-keys are shared by both steps, so keep them in this one file.
Rule: Keep exactly one saving caller per `runner.os` key. Callers set `with: restore-only: true` to read only; `master.yml` (Linux) and the Windows `cache-hf` step in `slow-tests.yml` remain save-enabled, because the Windows key is only populated by a save-enabled job.
Symptom: If a restore-only job is the only caller for a key, or a save-enabled job is the sole writer for a key that no save-enabled job runs for, the key is never populated after the dataset hash changes and every run downloads from Hugging Face again, risking 429 errors.
Constraints: Applies to any workflow that needs HF datasets in CI. Do not add restore-only to the only saving job for a runner.os; a new runner OS needs a save-enabled caller of its own.
applies: CI workflows under .github/ that use the cache-hf composite action; does not cover the Python test code or the HF library itself.
says: Automated tests are failing because of rate limit errors downloading external datasets.
Dataset downloads should be cached across test pipeline runs to prevent rate limits.
Test pipelines are re-downloading model datasets on every run instead of using cache.
Windows test runs fail with rate limit errors when fetching remote evaluation data.
Prevent secondary test jobs from overwriting the shared dataset cache used across pipelines.
search: The CI cache-hf composite action (.github/actions/cache-hf/action.yml) manages Hugging Face datasets caching (~/.cache/huggingface/hub/datasets--*) with an optional restore-only input to prevent 429 rate limits. When restore-only is true, it invokes actions/cache/restore without saving; otherwise it uses actions/cache with a key based on runner.os and the hash of tests/data/test_huggingface_dataset_and_source.py. Each runner.os key must have exactly one save-enabled job: master.yml saves for Linux and slow-tests.yml saves for Windows, while other callers set restore-only to true. If a key lacks a save-enabled caller, the cache is never populated after dataset changes, leading to repeated downloads and 429 errors; new runner operating systems require their own saving caller.
